payload.claim: The witness `tests/test_revert.py::test_revert_leaves_out_exactly_the_declared_renames_census_accepts` does not catch the spec's own wrong version #8 for criterion 1: 'The new name counted as collected at head when a head name starts with it, so the clause names a new name head never collected.' Broadening `new in after_set` (line 273) to a startswith/prefix match makes the mike pair ('t.py::test_mike_old' -> 't.py::test_mike') wrongly accepted, because 't.py::test_mike[1]' starts with 't.py::test_mike'. Because the bogus accepted new name is the literal string 't.py::test_mike' (never itself collected, only 't.py::test_mike[1]' is), subtracting it from `new_only` is a no-op, so `subset`/`expected_subset` is unaffected and the main assertion on the judged subset still passes. But `renamed_out = accepted_renames - declared` now contains 't.py::test_mike', so the note's rename clause names a new name the rule never actually collected at head - exactly the defect the wrong version describes, and exactly what the acceptance criterion's 'no other pair's new name' sentence forbids. The test's `not_left_out` list only checks `'t.py::test_mike[1]'` (the real collected name, which never appears in the note either way) and never checks that the bare `'t.py::test_mike'` string is absent from the note, so this wrong version passes the witness silently. A host-filed criterion probe already surfaced this exact mutation (file:line 273, text 'The new name counted as collected at head when a head name starts with it...') and the implementer's rebuttal argued it away by observing only that the *subset* is unaffected, without noticing the note/summary text itself differs - an argument that does not establish behavioural equivalence, only that this one witness fails to observe the difference.
